The '''1985–86 season''' was '''Real Madrid Club de Fútbol's''' 84th season in existence and the club's 55th consecutive season in the top flight of Spanish football.

== Season ==
During summer new president [[Ramon Mendoza]] appointed [[Luis Molowny]] as the club manager for the season after a failed bid on [[Athletic Bilbao]] coach [[Javier Clemente]] who clinched the league trophies in the [[1982–83 La Liga|1982–83]] and [[1983–84 La Liga|1983–84]] seasons and rejected the offer due to his contract expires in June 1986. Surprisingly, Clemente left the Lions midway through the [[1985–86 La Liga|1985–86 season]], after a run-in with star player [[Manuel Sarabia]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://elpais.com/diario/1986/01/21/deportes/506646009_850215.html|title=El enfrentamiento Clemente-Sarabia reúne dos días seguidos a la directiva del {{sic|nolink=y|Athlétic}}|trans-title=Clemente-Sarabia run-in has Athletic board of directors in two-day meeting|newspaper=El País|first=Patxo|last=Unzueta|language=es|date=21 January 1986|access-date=19 November 2013}}</ref> but, by that time, club president Mendoza signed an agreement for the upcoming season with Dutch coach [[Leo Beenhakker]]. After six years without winning La Liga, Real Madrid Club de Fútbol finally won the title in the 1985–86 season. The team also triumphed in the UEFA Cup, making it a European Double. Following a change in the chairman office (from [[Luis de Carlos]] to [[Ramón Mendoza]]), Real Madrid signed new top players (such as [[Hugo Sánchez]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/2012/10/14/mas_futbol/1350196008_850215.html|publisher=as.com|title=The 'Bridge Transfer' of Hugo Sanchez to Real Madrid: In 9 days was transferred out from Atletico to UNAM and to Real Madrid|author=Javier Hernandez|date=14 October 2012|accessdate=14 February 2025|language=es}}</ref> [[Rafael Gordillo]] and [[Antonio Maceda]]) under manager [[Luis Molowny]], and produced an emphatic season. This was the club's 21st league title in history and its second consecutive UEFA Cup. Real Madrid defeated [[1. FC Köln]] in the final to win the [[1985–86 UEFA Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|publisher=[[El País]]|title=El Madrid gana la Copa de la UEFA por segundo año consecutivo|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1986/05/07/portada/515800801_850215.html|language=es|date=7 May 1986}}</ref> The club were eliminated from the [[Copa del Rey]] by [[Real Zaragoza]] in the semi-finals.<ref>{{cite news|publisher=El País|title=El campeon de Liga, eliminado pese a su victoria|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1986/04/10/deportes/513468012_850215.html|language=es|date=10 April 1986}}</ref>
